questions.text: Is the PUSH4 bytes counted in BYTE_COUNT (so BYTE_COUNT = 4 after both)? (Scenario: On the same clock edge that h_we is asserted for a PUSH4 write, a second h_we write to INIT is not possible; instead, INIT is written on clock k and a PUSH4 is written on clock k+1.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. INIT written on clock k takes effect in the clock after, and only a push in that same clock is dropped. The PUSH4 written on clock k+1 is a normal push, so it is counted and BYTE_COUNT reads 4 afterwards (assuming no other pushes).
questions.evidence: - INIT written takes effect in the clock after the write and clears CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES; it wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock (the push is dropped).

questions.text: What does the unmapped read return, and are CRC and SCRATCH unchanged? (Scenario: Host writes 0xDEADBEEF to an unmapped address, then reads that address, then reads CRC and SCRATCH.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: The unmapped read returns 0. The write of 0xDEADBEEF to the unmapped address is ignored, so CRC and SCRATCH are unchanged by it.
questions.evidence: - Writes to read-only registers are ignored. Unmapped addresses read 0.

questions.text: Does h_rdata show 0x77 (not the old value)? (Scenario: Write of SCRATCH=0x77 with h_we at clock k, and h_re of SCRATCH at clock k+1.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. The write takes effect in the clock after h_we, so SCRATCH already holds 0x77 in clock k+1. A read in that clock must show the addressed register, so h_rdata shows 0x77 and not the old value.
questions.evidence: A write takes effect the clock after `h_we`. After `h_re`, `h_rdata` must show the addressed register within 2 clocks and hold it.

questions.text: Is CRC read as 0x00000000 (as for INIT with no push) rather than 0xFFFFFFFF? (Scenario: Immediately after rst deasserts following power-up, with no INIT issued and no writes, the host reads CRC, BYTE_COUNT, BUSY_CYCLES and SCRATCH.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: After reset with no INIT and no writes, CRC reads 0x00000000, not 0xFFFFFFFF. The internal CRC state is 0xFFFFFFFF and the final XOR is applied on read. BYTE_COUNT reads 0 and BUSY_CYCLES reads 0. SCRATCH reads 0, because it resets to 0.
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What is BYTE_COUNT after this write? (Scenario: After INIT, PUSH_N is written with TAIL_LEN=0 and data word 0xAABBCCDD.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BYTE_COUNT stays 0. With TAIL_LEN 0, PUSH_N pushes nothing, so BYTE_COUNT does not change (and BUSY_CYCLES does not count it either).
questions.evidence: with TAIL_LEN 0 it pushes nothing and BYTE_COUNT does not change.

questions.text: How many bytes are added to BYTE_COUNT? (Scenario: PUSH_N is written with TAIL_LEN=5 (field wider than 0..3) and data word 0x11223344, after INIT.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: 1 byte. TAIL_LEN stores only bits 1:0, so writing 5 (0b101) stores 1. PUSH_N then pushes only the low byte (0x44) of 0x11223344, and BYTE_COUNT increases by 1.
questions.evidence: TAIL_LEN values above 3 cannot be written: the upper bits are ignored (only bits 1:0 are stored).

questions.text: What value does BUSY_CYCLES read (the requirements fix N only for no-tail messages)? (Scenario: After INIT, 3 PUSH4 writes then one PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN=2 are issued, then BUSY_CYCLES is read after the datapath is idle.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BUSY_CYCLES reads 4. Each of the 3 PUSH4 writes counts one busy cycle, and the PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN=2 (N>0) counts one more.
questions.evidence: BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: After reset, what does SCRATCH read? (Scenario: SCRATCH holds 0x1234 and 10 PUSH4 writes are done with BYTE_COUNT=40; rst asserts for the MMCM-lock-plus-8-clock sequence mid-stream during the 6th push, then deasserts.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: SCRATCH reads 0x00000000 after reset. The 0x1234 written before the reset is lost, because SCRATCH resets to 0.
questions.evidence: | 0x008 | SCRATCH | RW | 32 bits, reads back what was written, resets to 0 |

questions.text: Is BYTE_COUNT reset to 0 by rst (without needing INIT)? (Scenario: Same mid-stream reset during the 6th PUSH4 with no INIT afterwards; host reads BYTE_COUNT and CRC.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. On reset BYTE_COUNT is 0 and the CRC state returns to the start value 0xFFFFFFFF, so CRC reads 0x00000000. No INIT is needed after the reset. The 6th PUSH4 that was in progress during reset is not counted.
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What does BUSY_CYCLES read? (Scenario: 1000 PUSH4 writes issued on 1000 consecutive clocks after INIT, then BUSY_CYCLES is read when idle.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BUSY_CYCLES reads 1000. It counts one per clock in which a push is processed, and PUSH4 on 1000 consecutive clocks gives 1000 busy cycles. The engine accepts one push per clock with no gaps, so a message of N full words takes N busy cycles.
questions.evidence: - BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: What does BYTE_COUNT read? (Scenario: BYTE_COUNT is at 0xFFFFFFFC after pushes, then one more PUSH4 is made.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BYTE_COUNT wraps around as a 32-bit counter, so after one more PUSH4 at 0xFFFFFFFC it reads 0x00000000.

questions.text: What does BUSY_CYCLES read? (Scenario: After INIT, PUSH4 of one word, then PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 2 and data 0x0000AABB, then PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 0. BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES are read.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: BUSY_CYCLES reads 2 (BYTE_COUNT reads 6). The PUSH4 counts one busy cycle and the PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 2 counts one busy cycle. The PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 0 pushes nothing and does not count, so it adds 0 to BUSY_CYCLES and 0 to BYTE_COUNT.
questions.evidence: BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: Is the CRC equal to zlib.crc32 of the bytes 01 00 00 00? (Scenario: Design powers up, reset releases, no INIT is written, and one PUSH4 of 0x00000001 is then written. CRC is read.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. Reset puts the CRC state at the start value 0xFFFFFFFF, so with no INIT a PUSH4 of 0x00000001 (bytes 01 00 00 00) reads back as zlib.crc32 of those bytes, with the final XOR applied on read.
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.
